They laugh and say, "This is what you get" as if it's some kind of joke for me showing minimal PDA with my boyfriend in our own room. I'm confused because we're not doing anything out of the ordinary. We're just watching TV, but the door being open makes me uncomfortable. People walk by in the dorm hallway, and I don't want them to see us. It feels like they're intentionally doing this to make me feel that way. Tonight, they left the room giggling and said, "Good luck" as they left the door open again. They do this multiple times an hour, like five times or more. Each time, I get up and close the door. I'm really tired of it, especially on their sixth trip in and out. So, I decided to lock the door. I know she has the key, but I thought if I have to go through the hassle of getting up to close the door, they can go through the hassle of unlocking it. Then, on their seventh trip, the friend comes and can't open the door. She starts banging on it really hard. I don't open the door because she knew what she was doing. She went back to where she and my roommate were hanging out and got the key, then came back in. She then told me it was very rude of me to lock the door because "it's my roommate's room." I calmly explained that if they're going to make me get up and close the door, they can go through the process of unlocking it. My boyfriend also asked why they were acting so passive-aggressive for no reason. She laughed and called me disrespectful again and left, leaving the door wide open. Now, I'm wondering if I'm really the asshole for just wanting my door kept closed so everyone passing by doesn't see me in my bed. First, I need to consider the dynamics of shared living spaces. On the other hand, locking the door might be seen as an overreaction, especially if the roommate has a key. It could escalate tensions between us. I also need to think about communication. Did I address the issue calmly and clearly? It seems like I did, but the other person's reaction was hostile. Maybe there's a middle ground, like talking to the roommate about setting some boundaries regarding the door. I also wonder about the intention behind their actions. Are they trying to provoke me, or are they just being inconsiderate? Overall, I feel like I was within my rights to want privacy, but locking the door might have been a bit harsh. Perhaps there's a better way to handle the situation without escalating it.
